items.title: Live: Israel will remain in Lebanon during 'temporary' ceasefire, Netanyahu says
items.description: The US State Department says a 10-day ceasefire beginning at 7am AEST will enable negotiations toward a permanent security and peace agreement. Follow live.

items.title: A 10-day ceasefire in Lebanon looms: What to know today
items.description: Israel and Lebanon agree to a 10-day ceasefire, but Israel's military will remain on Lebanese territory, meaning Hezbollah's conditions were not met.

items.title: PM rules out buying Russian, Iranian oil as countries scramble for supplies
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese insists Australia's sanctions on Russia and Iran will remain in place as the world scrambles to secure oil supplies amid a global crisis triggered by the Strait of Hormuz blockade.

items.title: Fears of another lockdown amid fuel shortages and recession risk
items.description: As fuel costs surge and supply fears grow, businesses and households say the economic shock from the war in the Middle East is already hitting home.

items.title: Pope blasts 'tyrants' spending big on war following public spat with Trump
items.description: The US-born pope has praised peace movements and peace makers during his visit to the African nation of Cameroon as the rift with US President Donald Trump intensifies.

items.title: In charts: A look at Australia's record spending on defence
items.description: The Defence Department reveals where the money will be going as Australia plans to spend a record $425 billion over the next decade.

items.title: Unpacking the 'war zone' after Geelong's refinery fire
items.description: The "unprecedented" fire at one of the two remaining oil refineries in Australia took more than 12 hours to extinguish. Here's what we know about how it unfolded.

items.title: 'Never thought we'd be homeless': Mother of 13 pleads for help
items.description: Finding a home for a large family in a regional area has left one family camping on the side of the highway in rural New South Wales. Nationally, Indigenous people are over-represented in homelessness statistics.

items.title: Australia is on the verge of aged care AI boom
items.description: Artificial intelligence-enabled robot companions, personal behaviour monitors and pain management apps could soon be used more widely within the sector.

items.title: Poor communication, no updates during oil refinery fire, residents claim
items.description: Geelong residents near an oil refinery fire have told a community meeting that initial information from emergency services was misleading and there was a lack of updates.

items.title: US alliance indispensable as Marles looks to build more self-sufficient ADF
items.description: Defence Minister Richard Marles has declared the United States alliance will remain indispensable for Australian national security even while Australia looks to build a more self-reliant defence force.

items.title: 100m litres of diesel secured under new powers, PM confirms
items.description: Anthony Albanese says that new powers allowing the federal government to underwrite the delivery of additional fuel cargoes have been used to purchase 100 million litres of diesel.

items.title: Bombs, rain and destruction: Life in Gaza six months into a ceasefire
items.description: Palestinians in Gaza fear they are being forgotten as the Iran war drags on, with Israeli strikes continuing despite a ceasefire and the humanitarian situation still dire.

items.title: Mandelson failed vetting but was given UK ambassador to US job anyway
items.description: Peter Mandelson was sacked from the role after revelations about his connections with the late sex offender became public.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: Trump's AI image, a 200m record and the Artemis II splashdown
items.description: It's Friday, and that means it's time to test your news knowledge from the past seven days. Were you paying attention this week?

items.title: Ephemeral nature of fungi has this photographer hooked on forest life
items.description: An exhibition bridges the gap between art and science by inviting visitors to imagine the world through the senses of other species and consider our own fragile relationship with nature.

items.title: Invasive species you should avoid — and what to plant instead
items.description: Agapanthus, morning glory or gazanias might be easy-growing plants in your home but their invasive nature can damage your garden and the environment. Here's what experts recommend.

items.title: Prince Harry tells summit he's 'felt lost, betrayed, or completely powerless’
items.description: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are back together in Melbourne after spending the second day of their Australian tour apart.

items.title: Trbojevic injures hamstring as Manly thrash Cowboys
items.description: The Sea Eagles have smashed North Queensland but the win has come at a heavy cost following a hamstring injury to star fullback Tom Trbojevic.

items.title: Daicos inspires Magpies to win as Blues youngster misses kick after siren
items.description: Nick Daicos stars in the final quarter to inspire Collingwood to a win as Carlton youngster Talor Byrne misses a kick after the siren to tie the scores.

items.title: Airport workers angered by surprise Qantas route cuts
items.description: Qantas's decision to cut one regional South Australian route and suspend four others came as a shock to workers at regional airports.

items.title: French president calls for ban on social media telling kids to read
items.description: Emmanuel Macron calls for a social media ban for children under 15, a monthly screen-free day for all, and urges high school students to switch off their phones.

items.title: How to tell if your dog is in pain and what to do if they are
items.description: New research suggests that many dog owners are not skilled in recognising pain in their pets.

items.title: Greyhounds ban a sticking point for Liberals and a sore point for Labor
items.description: The ban on greyhound racing in Tasmania was part of a deal made to keep the Rockliff Liberals in power. But getting that ban past parliament is proving to be a mongrel of a job. Meanwhile, Labor seems in denial over the issue.

items.title: Russia launches deadliest attack on Ukraine this year, killing 17
items.description: Russian forces have attacked the Ukrainian capital Kyiv and other cities, killing 17 people, as the defence leaders of more than 50 countries say they are aiming to send more aid to Ukraine.
